questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify what the income effect captures
questions.stem: Chef Maya raises flour price; which effect measures purchasing-power change?

options.text: The change in quantity demanded from changed purchasing power holding prices fixed
The change in quantity demanded from the price change alone holding utility fixed
options.misconception: confuses income effect with substitution effect

options.text: The change in total spending when both prices and income change together
options.misconception: confuses total effect with income effect

options.text: The change in quantity demanded from tastes changing over time

questions.explanation: The income effect isolates how changed purchasing power alters demand while prices stay fixed. The substitution effect instead holds utility fixed and changes relative prices.
questions.hint: Think purchasing power, not relative prices.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: What the Slutsky compensation holds fixed
questions.stem: Chef Leo's cost sheet shows flour 4 to 6 and income 100; what does Slutsky fix?

options.text: The original utility level at the new price ratio
The original consumption bundle's cost at new prices
The original purchasing power measured by old bundle cost at new prices
The new bundle's cost at old prices
options.misconception: swaps old and new price sets

questions.explanation: Slutsky compensation adjusts income so the old bundle still costs the same at new prices, holding old purchasing power fixed. Hicks instead holds utility fixed.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Explain why Hicks compensation differs from Slutsky for chef Nina's flour cost.

answer.exemplar: Hicks compensation adjusts income to keep the original utility level after the price change, while Slutsky keeps the cost of the original bundle fixed at new prices, so the two leave different purchasing power.

questions.explanation: Hicks holds utility constant, so compensation equals the equivalent variation. Slutsky holds the old bundle affordable, usually overcompensating or undercompensating relative to utility.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: State conditions for a Giffen good
questions.stem: Chef Omar sees rice price rise and quantity rise; income elasticity is -0.3 and budget share 0.6. Compute Giffen threshold?
questions.explanation: A Giffen good needs the income effect to outweigh the substitution effect, roughly |income elasticity| times budget share exceeding 1. Here 0.3*0.6=0.18, far below 1, so rice is not Giffen.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Chef Priya's Engel curve shows quantity 10 at income 100 and 16 at income 200. Find income elasticity.
questions.explanation: Income elasticity equals percent change in quantity divided by percent change in income: (6/10)/(100/100)=0.6. The exact log form gives 0.693. Both indicate a normal good.
